scope: Five grounded household, childcare and retail recovery candidates; no claim means no build authorized by this screen alone.
known_index_refresh: pipeline/refresh_known.sh completed:207 accepted,153 closed,134 pending,1700 rejected,217 revising;2411 total
method: Read current PR comments as well as state; primary manuals before simulator work; allow all safe shortcuts and no miniature people or isolated substitute fixtures.

candidates.title: Recover a receipt printer with its autocutter stranded across the cover opening
candidates.instruction: Get the receipt printer ready for the next customer.
candidates.fault: A visible paper jam leaves the cutter extended and mechanically prevents the roll cover opening.
candidates.mechanism: Epson TM-T88V: remove sliding cutter cover, manually turn cutter reset knob, release roll cover, remove jammed flexible paper and close the real latch.
candidates.primary_evidence: Manufacturer manual p13 documents cover access and reset knob; never force paper out. The manual shows the actual access direction, unlike a generic box.

nearest_prs.finding: Even receipt roll replacement is an occasional cashier/counter-worker chore, not core occupation work or an everyday firsthand scenario. Rigid attached paper and unlatched mock printer also invalid.

candidates.safest_shortcut: Power cycle might restore cutter automatically; manual recovery only needed when mechanical jam persists. Do not force manual reset in a scenario where power cycling solves it.

critic.importance: FAIL: explicit #2027 occupation-frequency rejection applies more strongly to less frequent cutter recovery.
critic.construct: Requires physically blocking cutter and deformable paper, actual small recessed knob access. No oversized knob.
critic.scoring: Observe blade retracted, paper free, cover latched and feed path clear; no turncount gate.
critic.feasibility: Small knob and paper jam expensive to reproduce faithfully; no reason to spend GPU after importance fails.

candidates.title: Free fabric caught under a sewing-machine needle plate
candidates.instruction: Remove the stuck fabric from the sewing machine.
candidates.fault: Fabric is drawn through the needle plate and held by tangled lower thread.
candidates.mechanism: Brother 888-J92 manufacturer troubleshooting: raise needle, remove foot/bobbin cover and cut tangled thread as needed; cloth and thread cause actual constraints.
candidates.primary_evidence: Manufacturer manual has the exact caught-fabric procedure and prohibits forcing removal when it fails; web FAQ403, complete primary PDF accessible.

nearest_prs.finding: Sewing operators/upholsterers/tailors/leather workers do not clearly reach500k US; specialist sewing procedure lacks broad firsthand familiarity.
Free lining caught in zip; different hardware but related tension-and-fabric recovery.

candidates.safest_shortcut: Cut accessible thread or remove needle/foot to remove cloth. These safe routes must be allowed; cannot demand a specific wheel/foot sequence.

critic.importance: FAIL under #1496; do not reclassify needle risk without an implicit credible human exposure.
critic.construct: Rigid cloth or grasp-triggered release would replace actual snag with a state machine.
critic.scoring: Practical fabric intactness and needle damage need validation, not mesh certificates.

candidates.title: Square and latch a feeding tray caught on only one booster-seat armrest
candidates.instruction: Put the feeding tray back square on the booster seat.
candidates.fault: One side is caught at an adjustment position; the other rests above its button.
candidates.mechanism: Mattel Fisher-Price CMH59 Healthy Care booster uses armrest buttons and three tray positions; exact manufacturer pictures identify both catches and release motion.
candidates.primary_evidence: CMH59 p6 shows snap-on tray buttons. Both manufacturers explicitly say tray is not a child restraint. A complete ordinary-scale booster would be needed, not isolated widened rails.

nearest_prs.finding: Click booster tray has both catches locked at second notch. Earlier revisions required rounded real tray and matching demo; no difference in core physical skill.
Scaled doll/carrier changes real geometry; unvalidated mesh harness assay not practical.

candidates.safest_shortcut: Fully remove tray and refit square. This is safe but is exactly the pending tray-latch skill; cannot require keeping one catch engaged.

critic.importance: FAIL novelty: recovery starting pose does not distinguish #1802.
critic.construct: Do not claim tray latch is fall restraint; manufacturer contradicts that. Preserve full-scale seat and actual button access.
critic.scoring: Both actual catches retained; permit any symmetric usable tray position unless user goal specifies one.
critic.feasibility: Plausible tabletop full booster but no build warranted because duplicate.

candidates.title: Release a loaded magnetic security-tag clutch at checkout
candidates.instruction: Remove the hard tag from this garment.
candidates.fault: Pin is under tension so clutch remains wedged even on detacher; ease load then extract pin while magnetic release is maintained.
candidates.mechanism: Sensormatic standard magnetic detacher guide specifies holding release bulb seated and pushing down then lifting clamp. Magnetic ball-clutch patents describe spring-biased pin capture.
candidates.primary_evidence: Manufacturer guide identifies compatible standard tags, excludes UltraTag, and documents two-handed continuous detacher seating. Patent is mechanism evidence, not dimensions of any arbitrary tag.

nearest_prs.finding: Same core task. Repeated reviews demand clutch physically reengage when detacher leaves and disallow late pull/reseat scoring exploit.

candidates.safest_shortcut: Push pin inward to unload then pull while tag remains seated. This is normal operation already covered by #1888, not distinct recovery.

critic.importance: FAIL exact near-duplicate of owned revising task.
critic.construct: No permanent magnetic-unlocked latch; restoring field must not retroactively validate pin travel.
critic.scoring: Actual pin retention and removal while clutch physically released.
critic.feasibility: Plausible but small ball-clutch geometry requires actual scale and force calibration.

candidates.title: Free a coin roll under a loaded till so a cash drawer latches
candidates.instruction: Close the cash drawer with the till and money inside.
candidates.fault: Proposed coin roll props one till corner above the inner drawer rim.
candidates.mechanism: APG documents inner-drawer removal to find obstructions and real spring latches; Vasario1313 has13x13inch footprint and removable till. No primary source verifies the proposed under-till coin-roll interference geometry.
candidates.primary_evidence: APG recommends removing inner drawer and checking obstruction, rails and latch spring. It does not mandate partial tilt of a loaded till or prohibit unloading.

nearest_prs.finding: Swap counted till into drawer, coins contained, close drawer. Removing till and replacing it is already owned.
Occasional till-adjacent maintenance not automatically core work just because cashiers are numerous.

candidates.safest_shortcut: Lift entire till out, remove roll, refit and close. Emptying coins first is also safe. Both erase proposed under-load maneuver; no rule may ban them.

critic.importance: FAIL shortcut and novelty; most legitimate work reduces to #2257 plus simple obstacle removal.
critic.construct: Exact roll-under-till contact unverified; do not fabricate a retaining lip or restrict whole till removal.
critic.scoring: No invented spill threshold from tilt or slide; actual coin containment only.
critic.feasibility: Ordinary33cm drawer fits but primary interior dimensions and latch geometry missing.

result.decision: None passes all importance, novelty and mechanism gates. No weak candidate built to meet quota.
